{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CffCFzwkKYx8TcMi6Sjrr","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The CUDA port is finished. Only `cahn_hilliard.cpp` and `CMakeLists.txt` were changed, and the executable is still `cahn_hilliard`. It always runs on the GPU, and if more than one GPU is visible it splits large grids across them.\n\n## Performance (4× RTX 3090, double precision)\n\n| Grid | Original CPU | CUDA |\n|---|---|---|\n| 128³ | 165 MCell/s | 16,600 MCell/s (2 GPUs) |\n| 256³ | — | 36,200 MCell/s (4 GPUs) |\n| 512³ | — | 43,600 MCell/s (4 GPUs) |\n| 768³ | — | 44,000 MCell/s (4 GPUs) |\n\nOne GPU reaches about 11,400 MCell/s. With 4 GPUs at 512³ it scales to about 3.8×.\n\n## What I did\n- **Build:** `CMakeLists.txt` now compiles the existing `.cpp` file as CUDA and targets the GPU architecture found at build time.\n- **Kernels:** one kernel computes the chemical potential and one does the update, with the same clamped boundaries as the original. Each GPU thread handles one column of the grid and steps through it, keeping the neighbouring values in registers.\n- **Arithmetic:** this card does double-precision math slowly, and that is the speed limit, not memory. So I combined the constant parts of the formula `4.5*((c+1)e_AA + (c-1)e_BB − 2c·e_AB) + 3c` ahead of time. The formula is mathematically the same and still works for any parameter values, and it gained about 25%.\n- **Multiple GPUs:** each GPU gets a slice of the grid along z, plus two extra boundary layers copied from its neighbours each step. The copies run while the GPUs compute the inner part of their slices.\n  - These GPUs can't copy directly to each other, so data passes through host memory.\n  - I put each buffer in the memory attached to the sending GPU's CPU socket. Before that, speed swung between 10 and 23 GCell/s depending on which socket the program happened to run on.\n- **How many GPUs:** 1 GPU below about 0.5M cells, 2 GPUs up to about 3M, then all visible GPUs. I tuned these cut-offs on this machine (two CPU sockets, PCIe), so other hardware may want different values.\n- **Timing:** the timer covers the same time-stepping loop as before. Setup and the final copy back to the host happen outside it.\n\n## Correctness checks\n- **Exactness of the GPU code:** before the formula change, a GPU build without fused multiply-add matched a CPU reference built the same way, bit for bit.\n- **Multi-GPU:** results on 1, 2, 3 and 4 GPUs are bit-identical across many grid shapes, including uneven ones (e.g. 100×37×61, 300×7×2000, 5×3×900).\n- **Against the original CPU program:** results agree to about 1e-15 even after 2000 steps. The tiny remaining difference is rounding: from the combined formula, and because the CPU and GPU compilers apply fused multiply-add differently. The original program's own output already changes with that compiler setting.\n- **Validation:** `-v` validation passes in all of these runs, including 1×1×1 and zero-step runs."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":301,"cache_read_input_tokens":77535,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":301},"output_tokens":813,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"3f040049-8823-4cc7-8195-e4b16eecedbc","uuid":"53373746-dc8f-400d-b4e4-7222d875b39a","timestamp":"2026-10-03T11:05:50.275Z","request_id":"req_011CffCFzYwMWMHt7Mmo6K7D"}
